hadiths.text: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
A good word is charity.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
The strong person is not the one who can wrestle, but the one who controls himself at the time of anger.
Make things easy, do not make things difficult. Give cheerfully and do not turn people away.
No fatigue, illness, sorrow, or grief afflicts a Muslim except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it.
The best charity is that given in Ramadan.
Whoever removes a hardship from a believer, Allah will remove a hardship from him on the Day of Judgment.
The example of the one who recites the Quran and the one who does not is like the example of a bag of musk and a bag of straw.
Fear Allah wherever you are, and follow a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out, and behave well towards people.
Avoid envy, for envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood.
He who does not thank people does not thank Allah.
Do not speak much without mentioning Allah, because too much speech without mentioning Allah hardens the heart.
The whole of a person is consumed by his tongue, except the one who controls it.
There is no Muslim who plants a tree or sows a seed and a bird, human, or animal eats from it, except that it is charity for him.
The most beloved of actions to Allah is the one that is continuous, even if small.
The best of people are those who benefit others.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.
The example of the five prayers is like a flowing river at the door of one of you, in which he bathes five times a day.
The prayer of the one who does not recite the Quran is incomplete.
The one who completes the Quran in less than three days does not understand it.
The one who memorizes the Quran will be crowned with a crown of light on the Day of Judgment.
The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
The one who recites the Quran and acts upon it will be given Paradise and his parents will be clothed with garments of light.
The fasting person has two joys: one at the time of breaking fast, and one at the meeting of his Lord.
The smell of the mouth of a fasting person is sweeter to Allah than the scent of musk.
Whoever stands in prayer during Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and hope, his previous sins will be forgiven.
The one who prays the night prayer will be granted a light in his heart.
The prayer of the one who has not purified himself is not accepted.
The best prayer after the obligatory is the night prayer.
The one who goes to the mosque to pray is like the one who goes out in the path of Allah.
The one who maintains ties of kinship will have his provision increased and his life prolonged.
The one who does not have mercy on our young and does not respect our elders is not one of us.
The best of you are those who are best to their wives.
The one who is kind to parents will be rewarded as if he performed Hajj and Umrah.
The one who prays for his parents without their knowledge will be rewarded abundantly.
The one who helps a poor person will be helped by Allah.
The one who feeds the hungry will be fed from Paradise.
The one who quenches the thirst of a believer will be quenched from the fountain of Paradise.
The one who visits the sick will be accompanied by angels.
The one who attends the funeral of a Muslim will be rewarded immensely.
The one who does not give charity for fear of poverty will remain in poverty.
The one who is generous to others will be given from the mercy of Allah.
The one who is patient will be given patience that no one else has.
The one who relies on Allah will be provided for from where he does not expect.
The one who is honest will be among the truthful.
The one who is humble will be raised by Allah.
The one who is arrogant will be lowered by Allah.
The one who loves for Allah will be with those he loves.
The one who fears Allah will be safe from the terror of the Day of Judgment.
The one who hopes in Allah will never be disappointed.
The one who trusts in Allah will be sufficient.
The one who is thankful will be given more.
The one who is patient will succeed.
The one who is content will be rich.
The one who is forgiving will be forgiven.
The one who is merciful will be shown mercy.
The one who is just will be justly rewarded.
The one who is kind will be treated kindly.
The one who is good to his neighbor will be rewarded.
The one who is good to his parents will have his sins forgiven.
The one who raises children with love will be protected from the Fire.
The one who educates his children will be rewarded.
The one who marries to protect his faith has completed half of his religion.
The one who is kind to his spouse will be rewarded.
The one who maintains family ties will be blessed.
The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever.
The most complete of the believers in faith are those with the best character.
Whoever guides someone to goodness will have a reward like the one who did it.
Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers.
A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not oppress him, nor does he leave him to be oppressed.
The one who does not memorize the Quran is like a ruined house.
Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and with the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
The best of you are those who are best to their families.
